traits.inflorescence.note: Watson and Dallwitz's account of the family, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): flowers aggregated in inflorescences (usually), or solitary; in racemes, in spikes, in heads, in corymbs and in panicles, the ultimate inflorescence units racemose. Read here as racemes most often, the racemose unit being the commonest whole inflorescence too.

traits.note: Abrams's Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States, volume 3 (1951), read in full: calyx 4- to 7-parted; flowers regular or slightly irregular, 4- or 5-merous; corolla sympetalous (but in two genera), urn-shaped in most, bell- or funnel-shaped in some; stamens usually twice as many as the corolla lobes; ovary superior, 2- to 4-lobed. Abrams keeps the blueberries apart (Vacciniaceae) for their inferior ovary. Watson and Dallwitz (as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read): ovary usually 4- or 5-locular.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 152 Ericaceae and 157 Vacciniaceae (blueberries and huckleberries), which APG joins as Ericaceae: shrubs or undershrubs, rarely trees; leaves mostly alternate, simple, mostly evergreen; stipules absent; fruit a capsule, berry or drupe.
